items.title: Linear-Time Non-Local Codec Placement for Machine Learning Model Compression
items.content: arXiv:2610.14703v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On-device inference imposes constraints on model storage and operand traffic and thus benefits from compressed operand representations, which mandate the use of encoding and decoding operators. However, na\"{\i}ve placement of codec operators can cancel the operand traffic gains sought from compression. In this work, I present an algorithm to place codec operators into a source computational graph to make it compatible with target hardware. The edges of the graph are colored so that each induced subgraph is weakly connected and has a maximal node that both postdominates all subgraph inputs and dominates all subgraph outputs; this unique node - dubbed the $\textit{absolute dominator}$ - is the natural location to observe the traffic flowing through the subgraph and learn parametric codec operators. The algorithm's time complexity is linear in the source graph's size. With respect to na\"{\i}ve local codec placement, the algorithm reduces modeled operand traffic by $24\%$-$44\%$ across four models, including $24\%$ on SigLIP and $34\%$ on SmolLM2.
items.author: Matteo Spallanzani
items.summary: The paper presents a linear-time graph algorithm for placing codec (encode/decode) operators in a computational graph so compressed operand representations remain compatible with target hardware. It introduces an absolute dominator notion via graph coloring to find natural observation points for traffic. This addresses the practical problem that naive codec placement can erase the traffic savings compression is meant to provide.
items.reasoning: Useful compiler/systems contribution for on-device inference compression with clean graph theory, but it is a single-author algorithmic paper whose practical impact depends on tooling adoption; moderate novelty within a niche.

items.title: How Shared Representations Become Specialized: Formation, Maintenance, and Latent Susceptibility
items.content: arXiv:2610.15830v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When several predictions use the same internal representation, information about some targets can remain easier to recover than information about others. We study how this specialization forms, persists, and changes in minimal artificial learners. With reconstruction errors weighted equally during learning, changing which target is observed precisely selects the favored target and redirects an already specialized learner. Removing current support can reduce a formed bias, whereas state-following update feedback can maintain it. We then compare learners formed through different observation and update conditions but matched on specified reconstruction measurements. Both change under the same brief opposing intervention, yet their responses differ. Resetting Adam largely removes the ten-update difference; exchanging its second moment reverses which route is more susceptible. New interventions show that equalizing the mean second-moment scaling reduces but does not remove the difference: its coordinate-wise pattern also matters. With fresh Adam or calibrated SGD, smaller route differences emerge later, whereas 500 common opposing updates bring the selected allocation endpoints close. A further control produces response differences with identical acquisition and equal mean loss weights but jointly different weight variability and realized sequence. Acquisition-selected formation also extends to a symmetric three-target setting. These interventions distinguish specialization's formation, present support, and time-dependent latent susceptibility.
items.author: Toru Takahashi
items.summary: Using minimal artificial learners, this study examines how shared internal representations become specialized across prediction targets, how such biases form, persist, and can be redirected. It shows matched learners with identical reconstruction measurements can respond differently to identical interventions, revealing latent differences not captured by surface metrics.
items.reasoning: Conceptually interesting theoretical work on representation specialization with possible interpretability implications, but abstract small-scale settings make real-world significance uncertain.

items.title: DeepFlow: Two Convergent Differentiable Approaches for Pairwise Conditional Random Fields
items.content: arXiv:2610.16546v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Basic probabilistic models form the basis of modern deep learning largely by defining the final activation layer of a network and allowing the networks outputs to be interpreted through a probabilistic lens. By increasing the complexity of these final activation layers to include features such as spatial regularisation, allow for these models to improve in performance without requiring significantly more data. The challenge however is to ensure that these more complex probabilistic graphical models adapt well to being used in tandem with deep learning, that is, ensuring they converge and have meaningful derivatives. The goal of this paper is to show two algorithms with provable convergence properties to allow this type of regularisation for image and signal classification models. Through both rigorous mathematical analysis and in silico experiments, we can show the differing performance between these solution types.
items.author: John S. H. Baxter
items.summary: The paper proposes two algorithms for integrating pairwise conditional random fields as structured output layers of neural networks, with provable convergence and well-defined derivatives. This enables spatial regularization in network outputs through a probabilistic graphical model lens without requiring substantially more data.
items.reasoning: Solid methodological work bridging probabilistic graphical models and deep learning with convergence proofs, but the approach addresses a well-studied problem and the incremental benefit over existing structured prediction methods is unclear from the abstract.

items.title: ACED: Reference-Anchored Aggregation of Natural-Language and Executable Evidence for Mathematical Reasoning
items.content: arXiv:2610.16635v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Natural-language self-consistency and executable programs provide complementary test-time evidence for mathematical reasoning, yet either channel may support the same semantic error. Thus we propose ACED, a reference-anchored framework that treats the self-consistency answer as the default and executable outputs as supporting evidence rather than interchangeable votes. ACED converts source-specific answer counts into smoothed supports, combines them through a weighted logarithmic pool, and overrides the reference only when a calibrated relative-evidence margin is exceeded. The same rule supports both candidate selection and admission of executable-only answers. Across five math word-problem benchmarks, ACED matches or outperforms the corresponding baselines. On GSM8K, ACED-CANDIDATE recovers 89.7% of the attainable candidate-set gain with only three damaging overrides, while ACED-ALL reaches 86.9% accuracy versus 82.6% for direct Program-of-Thought aggregation. These results show that preserving evidence provenance enables more reliable integration of natural-language and executable reasoning.

items.title: NBCLT: Parameter-Agnostic Norm-Ball Clipped Local Training
items.content: arXiv:2610.17913v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Distributed learning with multiple local steps reduces communication but aggravates drift, and its practical performance often depends on carefully tuned hyperparameters under heterogeneous data and communication constraints. At the same time, recent Muon-type optimizers suggest that constraining updates within suitable norm balls provides a simple way to encode geometric priors into optimization. In this work, we propose NBCLT (Norm-Ball Clipped Local Training), a unified local-training framework for both federated learning (FL) and decentralized learning (DL). NBCLT combines a predict-and-correct local update rule with Euclidean projections onto flexible norm balls, thereby performing norm-ball clipping under flexible update geometries while retaining a simple implementation. In FL, its problem-parameter-free regime achieves $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ communication complexity and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ total stochastic-gradient complexity without assuming bounded heterogeneity, when the per-round local-computation budget is scaled appropriately with the horizon. In DL, NBCLT is compatible with both static and time-varying mixing and preserves these accuracy exponents under the analogous computation scaling, up to fixed network constants and an additive initialization cost.
items.author: Linxuan Pan, Shucheng Yang, Junchi Yang
items.summary: NBCLT is a unified local-training framework for federated and decentralized learning that combines a predict-and-correct local update rule with Euclidean projections onto flexible norm balls, inspired by Muon-type optimizers that constrain updates geometrically. This controls client drift from multiple local steps while encoding geometric priors and reducing hyperparameter sensitivity under heterogeneous data. It works parameter-agnostically across optimization geometries.

items.title: Learning a Group Element from Its Action: Galois Correspondences, Optimal ERM, and an Abel-Ruffini Threshold for the Natarajan Dimension
items.content: arXiv:2610.18154v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study learning an unknown element $g$ of a group acting with finite orbits on a countable set, from examples $(x,gx)$. After a sample on $A$, the consistent hypotheses are the restrictions of a coset of the pointwise stabilizer of $A$, and the sample forces exactly the labels of points this stabilizer fixes; for a Galois group, they form the field generated by the data. Through this correspondence, multiclass dimensions become group invariants: the DS and graph dimensions equal the height, the Littlestone dimension the longest irredundant sequence length, and the teaching dimension the minimal base size. Among deterministic learners, symmetry makes empirical risk minimization optimal: on nondegenerate classes every consistent learner, whatever its tie-breaking, attains the optimal realizable sample complexity up to constant factors, and every consistent online learner the optimal mistake bound. Agnostically, every ERM's sample complexity exceeds the known lower bound by at most the DS-to-Natarajan ratio, up to constants. For finite Galois extensions of countable fields, the Natarajan dimension equals a group invariant, the coset-cube number, which is at least the number of complemented factors of any chief series of any subgroup. Hence the dimensions coincide for every solvable Galois group, while for the groups $A_5$ and $S_5$ of the quintic they are $2<3$ and $3<4$, and $A_5$ is the smallest group with a gap. For the Galois group $S_n$ of the general equation of degree $n$, they coincide exactly when $n\le 4$, i.e., in characteristic zero, exactly when the equation is solvable by radicals; the implication is one-way, as the simple group $\mathrm{PSL}(2,8)$ has no gap. For linear, orthogonal and unitary maps of $\mathbb R^d$ or $\mathbb C^d$ both dimensions equal $d$, and a two-fibered pseudo-cube is a disjoint union of Natarajan cubes exactly when its monodromy group is abelian.

It maps multiclass learning dimensions (DS, graph, Littlestone, teaching) to group invariants and proves ERM optimality among deterministic learners, with an Abel-Ruffini-type threshold.
items.reasoning: Elegant mathematics connecting group theory and statistical learning theory, which is intellectually interesting and could seed further work. However, it is abstract pure theory with no direct model or application impact in the near term.

items.title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
items.content: arXiv:2610.18280v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Advection-diffusion plays an essential role in transport phenomena such as atmospheric and cloud dynamics. Improved forecasting of cloud motion, in turn, enhances solar power production forecasts and facilitates the integration of additional photovoltaic (PV) sources into the power grid. However, both classical numerical models and emerging deep learning approaches face challenges when applied to spatially irregular sensor networks such as those formed by weather stations. In this work, we adopt a graph signal processing perspective and model advection-diffusion particles as signals on a graph to capture the dynamics of these processes. We introduce a Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network (PING) for forecasting future advection-diffusion particle concentrations on irregular grids. The model incorporates a discretized advection-diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the loss function to guide learning toward physically consistent solutions. This model is on par with state of the art models on synthetic and real transport phenomena datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index datasets. Furthermore, the PING model is successfully coupled with models for forecasting PV power production. This hybrid approach leverages data fusion from ground-based sensors at PV stations and satellite images with cloud concentration to improve the accuracy of intra-day PV power production.

It addresses the gap between classical numerical models and deep learning on irregular sensor layouts.

items.title: Learning When to Transfer: Reinforcement Learning for Carbon-Footprint Modeling in New Manufacturing Domains
items.content: arXiv:2610.18730v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Manufacturers often need to characterize a new material, process, or product before enough operating data are available to train reliable predictive models for this new, target domain. Existing manufacturing operations contain potentially useful knowledge to accelerate this characterization, but indiscriminate reuse of data from existing source domains can cause negative transfer in learning of the new, target domain when the manufacturing domains differ sufficiently. This work proposes a reinforcement-learning method for selective knowledge transfer, where its reward scores each opportunity to transfer against supervised alternatives, so negative transfer is avoided and controlled during forward prediction instead of being diagnosed afterwards. Given limited data from a new target domain, the learned policy chooses among predictors based on individual source operations, subsets of the sources, or the supervised alternatives: fully pooled sources, or target data alone. A validation gate deploys the transferred prediction only when it improves upon the supervised alternatives. The method is designed for learning variables supporting carbon accounting, as well as performance and quality outcomes. We demonstrate the approach by quantifying the embodied greenhouse-gas emissions of parts produced via material-extrusion additive manufacturing, using data from 729 experiments spanning five materials: ABS, PETG, TPU, PLA, and recycled PLA. The response combines measured fabrication electricity with polymer-specific cradle-to-gate production factors, while 22 material, process, and toolpath features characterize each experiment. In leave-one-material-out evaluation, this method achieves a mean test RMSE of 5.2 g CO2e per part, 20.00% lower than target-only training (32.5% lower when only 5-10% of the target training data are available) and 10.30% lower than indiscriminate source-target pooling.

items.title: Human Pose Estimation by Probabilistic Mixtures of Gaussian and Uniform Distributions
items.content: arXiv:2610.14093v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Despite advancements in sub-pixel decoding, modern Human Pose Estimation (HPE) architectures remain constrained by deterministic coordinate extraction from discrete heatmaps, which systematically fails under dense occlusions and Out-of-Distribution (OoD) ambiguities. To address these limitations, we propose a post-hoc continuous probabilistic framework that intercepts raw heatmaps and models them as a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) augmented with a spatially agnostic uniform distribution, requiring no architectural modifications or retraining. This continuous representation allows us to comprehensively explore the distinct contributions of density modeling to HPE. We show that the spatial expectation of our fitted GMM achieves precision parity with leading sub-pixel decoders without heuristic post-processing. Leveraging this continuous space, our test-time augmentation aggregates probability distributions rather than discrete activations, mitigating multi-scale heatmap poisoning. Furthermore, because our multimodal GMM parameterization isolates competing spatial hypotheses, it naturally interfaces with geometric regularizers such as Markov Random Fields. However, our analysis exposes the inherent vulnerabilities of 2D kinematic priors under perspective foreshortening and visual degradation. Crucially, this density formulation yields significant improvements in uncertainty quantification: our calibrated geometric covariance volume outperforms standard peak-intensity heuristics in OoD anomaly detection under severe occlusion. For in-distribution calibration, dynamically fusing our geometric metric via Adaptive Softmax reduces or matches baseline Area Under the Sparsification Error (AUSE) across benchmarks and degradation levels. Finally, we establish that this continuous parameterization is extensible to multi-view 3D architectures, bypassing the $\mathcal{O}(N^3)$ voxel memory bottleneck.

items.title: Decomposing A Neural Learner
items.content: arXiv:2610.14388v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Neural learners for classification and regression are often criticized as black boxes. We propose a probabilistic decomposition of neural learners that accounts for heterogeneous predictability across the feature space. A training procedure combining the EM algorithm, stochastic gradient descent, and maximum likelihood estimation is developed to jointly learn the predictable component and an input-dependent reliability score. We show that the optimal decomposed learner recovers the response distribution within the predictable component, while the reliability score characterizes the predictability of individual observations. We further extend the framework to incorporate localized feature transformations. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

items.title: Rethinking Opinion Measurement Interfaces for Human-in-the-Loop Optimization
items.content: arXiv:2610.14757v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Human-in-the-loop optimization refers to systems that present choices to a human decision-maker and query their judgment to optimize system parameters iteratively. The user interface typically provides either an absolute rating scale or asks for a preferred option. However, these approaches can potentially suffer from calibration problems, inconsistencies, and completeness violations of user preferences in such a sequential evaluation. This paper revisits the design space of opinion measurement interfaces for human-in-the-loop optimization. We conducted a study (N=360) using text summarization and image color enhancement tasks to evaluate human sequential feedback in six representative opinion measurement interfaces. Based on our analysis, we recommend using a listwise approach to support sequential opinion measurement, which counterweighs individual rating and preferential choice limitations and conveys more information for subsequent use. We further discuss the trade-offs in different user interface designs and provide guidelines to inform future research.

Findings inform how human preference data quality depends on interface design.

items.title: Energy-Guided Learning for Heat Equation with Noisy Source: Optimal Estimation and Generalization Bounds
items.content: arXiv:2610.15111v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Data and the governing partial differential equations (PDEs) of continuous-time dynamical systems provide rich structure for statistical learning. A central challenge is how to integrate data with PDE constraints in a principled way to improve generalization. In this paper, we characterize the statistical estimation and generalization properties of learning solutions to the heat equation with a noisy source function from finite, randomly sampled data. We first derive a novel variational formulation, which we characterize as the minimizer of loss function for an energy regularized and ellipticity debiased Sobolev regression. By formulating the learning task as a supervised problem over space-time domains under physically meaningful norms, our approach goes beyond the traditional supervised learning framework by effectively leveraging \emph{auxiliary data}---samples of the source function of the heat equation---to design a \emph{physics-informed energy regularization}. Our analysis reveals that learning in linear parabolic PDEs exhibits intrinsic anisotropy between spatial and temporal regularity, in sharp contrast to the static elliptic problems, leading to fundamentally different estimation and generalization behaviors. Specifically, we derive non-asymptotically rate-optimal estimation errors, as well as generalization error, which explicitly capture the interplay among temporal sampling, spatial resolution, and solution smoothness. Our numerical experiments demonstrate substantial orders of magnitude of reduction in testing errors against various physics-informed neural network methods on various parabolic and hyperbolic PDEs.

items.title: RF Fingerprinting of DSP Implementations using Machine Learning: An Over-the-Air Case Study
items.content: arXiv:2610.15494v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Radio frequency fingerprinting aims to identify transmitters by exploiting small differences in the emitted signal waveform. Common approaches exploit hardware-dependent imperfections for that purpose. This work instead investigates whether differences between digital signal processing implementations of a transmitter can be identified from their radiated signals. As a practical case study, five different software-based DSP implementations for generating a 2-FSK RTTY communication waveform are considered. In a monitoring receiver, a classifier can identify these DSP implementations using convolutional neural networks that are trained on augmented software-generated signals represented as raw IQ, power spectrum or instantaneous frequency. The trained networks are evaluated on over-the-air recordings obtained using a shortwave transceiver and a software-defined radio receiver. The best neural network combines IQ and the power spectrum representation and achieves an accuracy of up to 90%. The study further examines the influence of the signal SNR and the observation bandwidth on the classification accuracy. The results demonstrate that DSP implementations leave distinguishable characteristics in the transmitted signals and suggest that DSP-dependent fingerprinting can provide complementary information for specific emitter identification systems.

items.title: Regime-Aware Router Learning for Multi-Domain Medical Image Generation with Diffusion Experts
items.content: arXiv:2610.16082v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Heterogeneous medical image data motivate domain-specialized diffusion experts, but expert specialization alone does not determine how their predictions should be combined during sampling. Learning a global router is particularly challenging when the server has limited, potentially unrepresentative images. We study two router-learning strategies for a fixed expert pool. Server-Only learns input- and timestep-dependent expert assignments from server images with component labels. Anchor-Delta (AD) uses the same images and frozen experts to obtain additional evidence from denoising losses. It distills targets that combine this evidence with the current router's assignments, while a proxy gate controls a subsequent refinement step. Component labels describe data origin; expert losses measure empirical prediction performance. We evaluate these distinct signals through routing analyses and paired medical image generation. An AD-trained router improves generation metrics over Server-Only in a heterogeneous four-domain setting, and a separate server-data study shows gains in held-out routing over a corrected-routing comparator. Additional paired evaluations show that the effect of inference-time evidence mixing varies across benchmarks. These findings establish server-data availability and expert performance as distinct considerations in learning routers for multi-domain diffusion models.

A proxy gate controls a subsequent refinement step, addressing limited and unrepresentative server data.
items.reasoning: Practical mixture-of-experts style contribution for medical imaging with a sensible approach to data-constrained routing; moderately novel but scoped to medical image generation with limited shown generality.

items.title: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer
items.content: arXiv:2610.16199v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Freely swiveling casters are widely adopted in industrial AMRs/SDVs for their mechanical simplicity and load capacity. However, caster misalignment during low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers induces strong contact nonlinearities, widening the planning-execution gap between commanded $(v, \omega)$ and realized motion. Existing caster-aware strategies are highly sensitive to state-estimation reliability, causing unstable execution in uncertain transition regimes. To address this, we present Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control (MSC), a planning-execution integrated hierarchical framework featuring two core mechanisms. First, an uncertainty-aware NMPC (CU-MPC) dynamically schedules caster-aware costs and input regularization using predictive uncertainty to suppress overly aggressive maneuvers. Second, a reinforcement learning-based execution layer estimates and predicts caster states under partial observability, transforming high-level velocity commands into physically executable wheel speeds adapted to current contact conditions. Validations in Isaac Sim and real robots demonstrate that MSC offers a clear comparative advantage over existing decoupled compensation approaches by significantly improving caster-state estimation accuracy, minimizing misalignment, and enhancing tracking robustness in caster-sensitive maneuvers.

items.summary: MSC is a hierarchical planning-execution framework for autonomous mobile robots with freely swiveling casters, combining an uncertainty-aware nonlinear MPC with an RL-based execution layer. It targets the planning-execution gap caused by caster misalignment in low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers and improves robustness under state-estimation uncertainty.

items.title: QBFF: Deep Quantum Bottleneck for Automatic Speaker Verification Anti-Spoofing
items.content: arXiv:2610.16390v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A central goal of quantum machine learning is to identify applications in which small quantum circuits can improve task performance while remaining executable on real hardware. We investigate deepfake (synthetic) speech detection, a largely unexplored application in this area, where reliable confidence scores are as important as discrimination performance because deployment decisions are made at fixed thresholds and overconfident errors can be costly. We introduce QBFF, which routes a compressed speech representation through a small 8-qubit variational circuit (VQC) used as a drop-in bottleneck, with a matched classical bottleneck as the control. The quantum circuit yields better-calibrated confidence in most matched comparisons, including out-of-distribution evaluation, though the downstream deployment-cost benefit is model-dependent. We then run the same circuit on a real IBM quantum processor. To our knowledge, this is the first anti-spoofing pipeline to run on a QPU; hardware execution demonstrates feasibility, with lower subset EER and $C_{llr}$ but higher mean actDCF than the matched classical reference. Together, these results show that hardware-executable quantum bottlenecks can improve score reliability, with gains that vary by evaluation setting.

items.title: Amortized Variational Inference of Latent Intensities from Replicated Point Patterns
items.content: arXiv:2610.16669v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Bayesian inference for latent point process intensities often relies on per-dataset sampling or optimization, making repeated inference computationally expensive. We propose a neural-network-based amortized variational framework that learns a reusable inference rule mapping a variable number of replicated point patterns to a distribution over their shared latent intensity. Trained from event times using the point process likelihood, the model learns an amortized inference rule without ground-truth intensity supervision. At test time, it performs inference of the latent distribution in a forward pass. On synthetic data, additional realizations improve intensity recovery and yield narrower credible intervals with broadly stable coverage. Our method is tested on bicycle-sharing data and achieves the highest mean held-out log likelihood among the evaluated methods while requiring substantially less inference time than the Log-Gaussian Cox Process baseline.

items.title: Honeycomb Crystal in a Mass-Asymmetric Electron-Hole Bilayer
items.content: arXiv:2610.17030v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A two-dimensional electron gas in a uniform neutralizing background forms a triangular Wigner crystal at low density. In a strongly mass-asymmetric electron-hole bilayer, localized heavy holes instead provide a nonuniform positive background that supports an electron crystal at densities two orders of magnitude higher than for a homogeneous electron gas in the same material. Here we show that correlated mobile electrons can overturn the preference for triangular order, stabilizing a honeycomb electron-hole crystal. Using the powerful real-space neural-network variational Monte Carlo in the Born-Oppenheimer limit with fixed holes, we find that increasing the density drives a transition from a triangular electron-hole crystal to a honeycomb crystal, which eventually melts into itinerant electrons coexisting with the honeycomb or the triangular hole lattice at fixed interlayer separation. We further propose a BLG/hBN/WS$_2$-WSe$_2$ heterostructure as a platform for the predicted honeycomb crystal, at an experimentally feasible density $n\sim10^{11}~\text{cm}^{-2}$.

items.title: When Does Opponent Modeling Pay Off? Spatial Inference Stabilises Reinforcement Learning under Partial Observability
items.content: arXiv:2610.18229v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Deep reinforcement learning agents in partially observable competitive games must act on beliefs about an unseen opponent's intent. We study a spatial opponent model: a transformer trained with hindsight-relabelled opponent goals that outputs a subgoal heatmap from the opponent's observed trajectory, fused early into a dueling double DQN. In symmetric constant-sum foraging games with partial observability, the module stabilises training. Plain TD(0) DQN suffers degenerate seeds in three of four one-step configurations, whereas the opponent-model agent never collapses and, wherever training succeeds, recovers the majority of the symmetric game value. Transfers zero-shot to a foraging opponent unseen by the learner, with a positive goal advantage over the baseline, and loses this edge exactly where an information argument predicts: against a full-information tracking adversary whose intent is the learner itself, and on resource-dense maps where both agents saturate. A blindfold ablation, zeroing the heatmap at deployment, decomposes the advantage into two mechanisms: training-time stabilisation, which dominates where the credit assignment is hard and survives blinding on the dense map, and deployment-time inference, whose reliance shrinks as fog thins on the sparse map. We conclude that opponent-goal inference is a stability-and-transfer mechanism whose value is governed by measurable boundary conditions: visibility (fog thickness), opponent intent, and resource density.

items.title: AIRRI: Towards a Human-Readable, Machine-Resistant Reading Interface
items.content: arXiv:2610.18724v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The rapid advancement of image-to-text extraction systems and large language models (LLMs) poses new challenges for educational assessment by making assignment materials easy to transcribe and solve with minimal human effort. To address this problem, we present AIRRI (Artificial Intelligence Resilient Reading Interface), a framework for generating machine-resistant educational content, a dataset of higher-education assignments for evaluation, and an initial evaluation of the human readability of AIRRI machine-resistant text designs. AIRRI employs two categories of machine-resistance techniques. First, AIRRI applies image transformations including character spacing, word spacing, line spacing, character opacity variation, stripe overlays, and image noise. Second, AIRRI applies decision-based adversarial attacks: RayS, SurFree, and ADBA. We evaluate AIRRI against three image-to-text systems: Tesseract, EasyOCR, and the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our results show that AIRRI substantially degrades automated text extraction performance. AIRRI increased character error rates for EasyOCR (6.9% to 55.9%), Tesseract (2.3% to 100.0%), and GOT-OCR2 (30.7% to 48.1%). Word error rates increased for EasyOCR (24.9% to 96.7%) and Tesseract (10.7% to 100.0%). Among the evaluated decision-based attacks, ADBA consistently produced the largest degradation in image-to-text performance, while RayS and SurFree produced more moderate reductions. EasyOCR and Tesseract were generally more susceptible to both image-based and adversarial perturbations than the transformer-based GOT-OCR2 model. Our findings suggest that AIRRI can significantly reduce the reliability of image-to-text-to-LLM workflows, increasing the effort required for AI-assisted assignment completion.

items.title: Modeling the Arrival Time of Information-Bearing Events in Natural Language
items.content: arXiv:2610.14212v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Understanding how information is distributed over time is fundamental to modeling natural language. While existing empirical studies primarily rely on post-hoc analysis of information-theoretic metrics, such as surprisal, little is known about the generation processes under the surface. We propose a novel approach for addressing this gap using the tool of neural temporal point processes (TPPs) by modeling the key information-bearing events in text sequences with learnable event intensity functions. Our model takes the history of event intervals and the contextual semantic representations from LLMs as input, and predicts the future arrival times for two types of events: new-word and high-surprisal-token. The experimental results reveal an interesting distinction in event intensities: LLMs tend to produce new words at significantly higher rates than humans, while high-surprisal tokens do not exhibit the difference. A decaying pattern of intensity over time is found in new-word events for both humans and LLMs, but not in high-surprisal-token events. Our findings revisit and extend previous studies that use simpler methods; provide supplementary evidence for theories about constrained context representation inherent in human language production; and find a new angle to view human and LLM generation differences.

items.title: Evaluating Bias in Chinese Large Language Models across Tasks and Registers: Task Operationalization Effects and Irony Classification Risks
items.content: arXiv:2610.14464v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In Chinese content governance, large language models are increasingly used to identify toxic and discriminatory expressions, yet both task operationalization and ironic expression can alter bias measurement readings. We conducted a preregistered multi-task behavioral audit of multiple Chinese large language models. In the content classification experiment, the core panel's classification error rate rose from 10.9% in the formal register to 23.5% in the yinyang (an echoic-irony register) version, a risk difference of +12.7 percentage points. (95% CI [+9.7, +15.7]). Inter-rater agreement was lower in the yinyang register (majority-vote kappa = 0.299), so the increase contains a component of label uncertainty propagation, but the direction of increase was consistent under both adjudicated and majority-vote reference standards. Explicit irony-aware prompts reduced the intervention panel's error rate by 9.6 percentage points. We operationalized the 29 shared proposition anchors into three task forms: social consensus estimation (Form A), high-stakes decision (Form B), and controlled association rating (Form C); independent manipulation checks found that all 58 A-C comparison units received unanimous agreement, whereas the low A-B convergence was confirmed by calibrated majority adjudication (87.8% supporting the minority judgment); on the irony-probe materials, the interactions of B and C relative to A were +0.577 and +1.121, respectively. Thus, when evaluating large language models for Chinese content governance, the effect of task operationalization on bias readings is an empirical question that requires data to answer, and safety evaluation should incorporate the ironic register as a test condition.

items.title: PAT: A Personality-Driven Augmentation and Transfer Learning Framework for Depression Detection on Social Media
items.content: arXiv:2610.15044v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Depression is a prevalent mental disorder that affects millions worldwide, with early detection crucial for effective intervention. While exist?ing methods have achieved promising results in automated depression detection, they face two key limitations: (1) noise in post screening: symptom-based semantic screening is easily misled by superficial lexical patterns, thereby introducing false-positive posts; (2) weak op?timization of the post encoder: relying solely on coarse user-level supervision signals pre?vents models from capturing depressive cues within individual posts. To address these limita?tions, we propose PAT, a Personality-driven Augmentation and Transfer learning frame?work. In the first phase, PAT optimizes a post?level encoder via a fine-grained contrastive learning objective, utilizing LLM-based data augmentation driven by classic personality the?ories to alleviate data scarcity. In the second phase, the trained post-level scorer is deployed for high-quality post filtering, while its en?coder parameters are seamlessly transferred for user-level tasks. Extensive experiments demon?strate that PAT significantly outperforms exist?ing methods. Furthermore, PAT delivers multi?granular interpretability by tracing post-level mental-state trajectories and highlighting key symptoms, thereby offering reliable diagnostic evidence for clinical practice.

It first optimizes a post-level encoder before applying user-level supervision. The work targets earlier detection of depression, where automated screening can support timely intervention.

items.title: An Interpretable Linguistically-Grounded Analysis of Scene Saliency in Movie Screenplays
items.content: arXiv:2610.15544v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We investigate the factors affecting salience in movie screenplay by posing two research questions: 1. {\em Does Uniform Information Density (UID) predict salient scenes?} 2. {\em What other linguistic properties distinguish salient scenes from non-salient background?} We answer both questions through a controlled corpus study on the MENSA corpus, paired with a Linguistically-Grounded Salience Model (LGSM), a dual-stream classifier that fuses a frozen BERT encoder with explicit linguistic features through adaptive gating. The UID picture is layered in long-form discourse. Per-scene UID summaries carry no independent signal once length is controlled, but at the token level salient scenes match non-salient material in the bulk while specifically suppressing the rarest, hardest-to-predict tokens in the upper tail. UID therefore lives at the within-scene token level rather than as a per-scene aggregate. Salient scenes also show a moderate and sustained cast of central characters (following an inverted-U pattern), strong third-person usage, syntactically simpler language, and more abstract vocabulary about motivation and conflict. LGSM exploits this signature and improves recall on salient scenes over a strong semantic baseline while yielding better downstream summaries.

items.title: Lost in Contrast: Instruction-Preserving Decoding for Reliable Visual Question Answering
items.content: arXiv:2610.16722v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual contrastive decoding corrects answers using the prediction difference between the original image and a reference condition, yet the same contrast also turns supported abstentions into incorrect answers. We find that abstentions are lost at two stages: contrastive decoding with candidate filtering can exclude the abstention token before any comparison takes place, and the reference branch's response to the abstention instruction is removed when the reference prediction is subtracted. We therefore propose instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the effect of the abstention instruction on the original-image prediction intact while leaving the contrast strength freely adjustable. Using a perturbed image and an image-free prediction as references, we obtain IP-VCD and IP-M3ID. On decision utility (DU), which credits both correct answers and supported abstentions, both methods outperform all compared non-IP baselines on every one of nine models on VizWiz, and IP-VCD also leads on eight of nine models on Food-101. Candidate measurements and paired per-question comparisons show that computing the instruction effect and the visual contrast term separately lets contrastive decoding support both correct answers and supported abstentions.

It proposes instruction-preserving decoding, which keeps the abstention instruction's effect intact while allowing contrast strength to be freely adjusted. This improves reliability of abstention behavior, an important calibration property.

items.title: AD4EDU: Benchmarking University Lecture Audio Description across Accessibility Standards, Metrics, and Learner Preferences
items.content: arXiv:2610.17042v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Audio description (AD) aims to enhance the accessibility of visual media for blind and low-vision (BLV) persons. However, in higher education, where slide-based lectures are a default mode of teaching, lecture AD remains largely underexplored. The main reason is that existing production guidelines, evaluation metrics, and benchmark datasets are oriented toward entertainment content and do not transfer to lectures, where ADs must complement the lecturer's speech, resolve deictic references, and fit within narrow pauses. In this work, we propose AD4Edu, consisting of an AD benchmark, AD4Edu-Bench, and a rule-diagnosable evaluation metric, AD4Edu-Eval, for generating and evaluating ADs in higher education. Specifically, we consolidated established accessibility guidance, including WCAG 2.2, the DCMP Description Key, and NCAM's STEM description practices. We further collected silver reference ADs, judge-ordered preference pairs, and pairwise preferences from four BLV raters, and post-trained models with direct preference optimization (DPO) for detailed analysis. Our findings indicate that while the metric reliably detects violations of the standard, ADs that comply with it do not necessarily fulfill the subjective preferences of BLV persons, most notably on description length, underscoring the necessity of active participation of BLV persons in co-designing inclusive AI solutions.

The work consolidates accessibility standards and learner preferences into an evaluation framework.

items.title: Text-Only vs. Image-Aware VLM Judges for Manga Translation Evaluation
items.content: arXiv:2610.17908v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In manga translation, visual context outside speech-bubble text, including speaker identities, referents, and scene tone, is depicted in page images, making it natural to refer to images during translation evaluation. However, most conventional manga translation evaluations rely solely on text-only automatic metrics, leaving the impact of image input insufficiently explored. We propose a practical validation framework that employs the same vision-language model (VLM) as both a text-only judge (TOJ) and an image-aware judge (IAJ) to investigate evaluation divergences associated with image-aware evaluation procedures. We use a Japanese-English manga dataset of official translations aligned at the page and speech-bubble levels. First, adding page images to TOJ improved the primary VLM's detection of deliberately injected, visually dependent degradations. Second, we analyzed evaluation divergences between TOJ and IAJ, finding different error counts and error-category distributions. Human verification did not reveal a consistent preference between TOJ and IAJ.
items.author: Subaru Kimura, Jun Suzuki
items.summary: The paper compares text-only and image-aware VLM judges for evaluating manga translation, using the same vision-language model in both roles on a page- and speech-bubble-aligned Japanese-English dataset. It examines how visual context such as speaker identity and scene tone changes evaluation outcomes. The findings inform how multimodal evaluation should be conducted for visually grounded translation tasks.
items.reasoning: Useful empirical analysis of an understudied evaluation question with a well-aligned dataset, but scoped to manga translation and relies on a single VLM as both judge variants, limiting generalizability.

items.title: DSM-Free UAV Visual Localization via Latent-Depth Variable Projection and Structure-Adaptive Coupling
items.content: arXiv:2610.14945v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Visual localization enables unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to maintain absolute positioning in GNSS-denied environments. A common approach matches UAV images with geo-tagged orthographic maps and estimates camera pose using Perspective-n-Point (PnP) with elevations from Digital Surface Models (DSMs). However, accurate and up-to-date DSMs are often unavailable in practice. Orthographic-perspective geometry (OPG) enables DSM-free localization in scenes with varying elevations, yet existing methods typically estimate pose indirectly through intermediate matrix estimation and decomposition. To address this limitation, we propose Latent-Depth Variable Projection (LDVP), which treats the unknown scales along perspective viewing rays as latent depths. By analytically eliminating these depths and solving for the horizontal camera center in closed form given the rotation, LDVP reduces nonlinear estimation to a rotation-only problem, enabling direct recovery of metric horizontal position without assuming a planar scene. To improve localization robustness across different scene structures, we further introduce Structure-Adaptive Coupling (SAC), which uses relative scene structure inferred from monocular depth estimation to select LDVP when the matched points are not dominated by a single plane, and Planar-PnP otherwise. Our local observability analysis reveals how scene elevation variation affects the geometric constraints of OPG, providing a basis for this adaptive strategy. Extensive experiments show that LDVP consistently outperforms existing OPG-based DSM-free methods, while SAC further improves robustness across diverse scenes and substantially narrows the gap to DSM-based localization. Code will be released at https://github.com/UAV-AVL/LDVP-SAC.

items.reasoning: Removing DSM dependency is a practical improvement for map-based drone localization, and the latent-depth variable projection formulation is technically clean. The scope is specialized and the approach is an incremental advance within UAV localization.

items.title: Retraining-Free Depth Pruning of Vision Transformers: A Cross Domain Study of Layer Redundancy
items.content: arXiv:2610.15005v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Transformer architectures have achieved strong results in natural language processing and computer vision, but their deployment is limited by high computational, memory and storage costs, motivating research into model compression techniques, such as pruning, while preserving performance. Prior work has shown substantial redundancy in large language models (LLMs), and redundancy in vision transformers has also been investigated, but it remains less systematically analyzed than in LLMs. In this work, we extend similarity-based redundancy analysis to vision models by measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify transformations with minimal impact. We study redundancy patterns across several transformer architectures and find that deep vision transformers such as DINOv2 and SwinV2, like language models, exhibit significant redundancy. We then evaluate how this redundancy can be exploited to improve efficiency, analyzing the trade-off between inference speed and performance degradation under different pruning strategies. Our results show that moderate pruning can yield substantial acceleration with limited impact on accuracy, and that 20% of the DINOv2 blocks can be removed without any retraining, for a 1.24x throughput gain and a 20% lower energy per image at a relative accuracy loss below 1% on ImageNet-1K. We further propose a model selection pipeline that automatically identifies the best pruned configuration for a given dataset, reducing FLOPs by 13% to 27% on average across architectures with an average accuracy change between -0.3 and +1.0 points.
items.author: Alessandro Viespoli, Loris Nanni
items.summary: The authors extend similarity-based redundancy analysis from LLMs to vision transformers, measuring cosine similarity between layer inputs and outputs to identify low-impact transformations suitable for retraining-free depth pruning. The cross-architecture, cross-domain study systematically characterizes redundancy patterns in vision models.
items.reasoning: Efficiency research on ViTs is valuable, and the cross-domain empirical study of redundancy fills a gap relative to the LLM literature. The core technique (input-output similarity pruning) is established, so this is a solid analysis rather than a breakthrough.

items.title: Rethinking Supervision in Document Unwarping: A Self-consistent Flow-free Approach
items.content: arXiv:2610.15445v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In recent years, the proliferation of smartphones has led to an upsurge in the digitization of document files via these portable devices. However, images captured by smartphones often suffer from distortions, thereby negatively affecting digital preservation and downstream applications. To address this issue, we introduce DRNet, a novel deep network for document image rectification. Our approach is based on three key designs. Firstly, we exploit the intrinsic geometric consistency inherent in document images to guide the learning process of distortion rectification. Secondly, we design a coarse-to-fine rectification network to leverage the representations derived from the distorted document image, thereby enhancing the rectification result. Thirdly, we propose a unique perspective for supervising the learning of rectification networks, where undistorted document images are employed for supervision, which is free of warping mesh as ground truth in existing methods. Technically, both low-level pixel alignment and high-level semantic alignment jointly contribute to the learning of the mapping relationship between deformed document images and distortion-free ones. We evaluate our method on the challenging DocUNet Benchmark dataset, where it sets a series of state-of-the-art records, demonstrating the superiority of our approach compared to existing learning-based solutions. Additionally, we conduct a comprehensive series of ablation experiments to further validate the effectiveness and merits of our method.
items.author: Shaokai Liu, Hao Feng, Wengang Zhou
items.summary: DRNet is a deep network for document image rectification that exploits intrinsic geometric consistency instead of dense flow-based supervision, using a coarse-to-fine architecture built on representations of the distorted image. It targets smartphone-captured documents with warp distortions that hurt digitization.
items.reasoning: A thoughtful reframing of supervision in document rectification that reduces annotation dependence and could improve practical OCR pipelines; niche task with solid but not high-impact methodological contribution.

items.title: From Sound to Sense: An Anatomy of Semantic Supervision for Speech-Driven Visual Grounding in Remote Sensing Imagery
items.content: arXiv:2610.16364v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speech-driven visual grounding in remote sensing (RSVG) removes the typing bottleneck of text-based interaction and is intended to preserve prosodic intent, enabling hands-free target acquisition in time-critical missions. The direct-audio paradigm, mapping raw speech straight to a bounding box and bypassing automatic speech recognition (ASR), was recently adopted by RSTalker, but what such grounders actually learn about language remains unmeasured. SemEcho grafts a frozen Whisper speech pathway onto a VLTVG grounding host so that speech and text share one decoder, making the paired text, free by construction since speech corpora in this task are synthesized from DIOR-RSVG expressions, a training-time teacher and a fair, same-host text upper bound. On this instrument we dissect three semantic injection channels (feature-mimicry distillation, word-level CTC supervision, and two-stage ASR pretraining) with linear semantic probes, and release Audio-DIOR-R (80,973 training clips; 10 timbres x K=3; Qwen3-TTS synthesis with online sox noise lambda in [0, 0.4]) and Audio-DIOR-Comp, a re-split holding out 17 attribute-category combinations under a 2x2 acoustic-semantic protocol. Our anatomy yields four findings. (i) Whether direct alignment beats a domain-trained ASR cascade is decided by recognizer quality: against a weak in-domain cascade (CTC 0.53) direct wins by 9.0 Acc@0.5 points with transcription errors concentrated on spatial-relation words, but a strong in-domain cascade (CTC 0.029) reaches the text upper bound (80.8 vs. 81.0) and beats even the strongest direct model by 8.8 points; the anti-ASR premise holds only against weak recognizers.
items.author: Zhongyu Pang
items.summary: Analyzes what direct-audio speech-driven visual grounding models actually learn about language, grafting a frozen Whisper pathway onto a VLTVG grounding host in SemEcho so speech and text share one decoder, with synthesized text serving as a training-time teacher and same-host upper bound. The work measures semantic supervision quality for hands-free target acquisition in remote sensing.
items.reasoning: A careful analytical study in a fairly narrow intersection of speech input and remote-sensing grounding, with a clean experimental design that separates audio and text pathways. Value is real for the speech-driven RSVG niche and for understanding modality transfer, but the scope and single-solo-author setting limit broad impact.

items.title: Revisiting Natural Language Prompts from Large Language Models for Open-Vocabulary Video Recognition
items.content: arXiv:2610.16666v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) like CLIP have shown great success in image tasks, however, applying CLIP to open-vocabulary video recognition poses challenges. Due to the limited text information, directly fine-tuning CLIP on video recognition datasets may lead to overfitting and hinder its generalizability. A prevalent method is to enrich text information by generating prompts using Large Language Models (LLMs). However, limited efforts have been made to explore how to generate higher-quality prompts that can contribute to classify unseen categories, and how to further enhance vision-text alignment based on these prompts. In this paper, we propose P2CLIP (Prompt-guided CLIP), which aims to bridge this gap by exploring the impact of prompts across three aspects: category, video, and frame. At the category level, we argue that LLM-generated prompts under simple instructions may suffer from semantic overgeneralization, which can blur the category boundaries and hinder the performance of the model. To address this issue, we design Generic-Discriminative Prompt using LLMs to obtain discriminative category embeddings with rich semantic information. At the video and frame levels, we first use VLM and LLM to generate frame and video descriptions for enhancing vision-text alignment. Then we propose a Knowledge-Guided Temporal Aggregation mechanism, which leverages the expert knowledge derived from LLMs to guide the temporal modeling of videos and encourage a better construction of the joint visual-textual feature space. Extensive experiments across various benchmarks, including zero-shot and few-shot settings, demonstrate the effectiveness of our method.

items.summary: P2CLIP investigates how LLM-generated prompts affect open-vocabulary video recognition with CLIP-style models, exploring how to generate higher-quality prompts for unseen categories and how to improve vision-text alignment using them. It aims to reduce overfitting from direct fine-tuning on limited video text information.
items.reasoning: A reasonable, systematic study of prompt generation for open-vocabulary video classification, but prompt engineering for CLIP is a well-trodden area and the contribution appears as a refinement rather than a significant advance.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Multimodal Brain Tumor Segmentation With Stage-Wise Shared Adapters
items.content: arXiv:2610.18571v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Different MRI modalities reveal different parts of a brain tumor. Segmentation models combine information from these modalities to outline tumor regions. Many models use a separate encoder for each modality. However, exchanging features among these encoders at several stages can increase model complexity. We introduce the Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), which combines compressed features from the modality encoders in a shared path and returns adapted features to each stream. In its fixed-blending form, BWSA adds the adapted features to the original features. Its trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) instead learns separate weights for the original and adapted features at each modality and encoder stage. We evaluate both variants on BraTS 2020 and BraTS 2023 with four segmentation backbones. On the official BraTS 2023 online validation set, BWSA increases average region-wise Dice by 1.3--7.6 percentage points relative to the corresponding unmodified backbones. TG-BWSA increases it by 2.8--7.7 points. Both variants add approximately 0.85--3.73% parameters and reduce average HD95 relative to the unmodified backbones.
items.author: Milad Rostamian, Mohammadreza Mohammadi, Ender Konukoglu, Mohsen Soryani
items.summary: The paper introduces Block-Wise Shared Adapter (BWSA), a parameter-efficient mechanism for exchanging features across per-modality MRI encoders at multiple stages, with a trainable-gated variant (TG-BWSA) that learns per-stage blending weights. Evaluated on BraTS 2020, it targets reducing model complexity in multimodal brain tumor segmentation while maintaining accuracy.
items.reasoning: Solid parameter-efficiency contribution in an important medical imaging application. The adapter design is incremental rather than conceptually novel, but the stage-wise gating idea is sensible and well-motivated, with credible authors in the field.

items.title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
items.content: arXiv:2610.18741v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting, where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limits their effectiveness and reliability. Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time. Considering this, we propose a novel context-aware multimodal late fusion approach that integrates a lightweight gating network within our probabilistic calibration framework. The gating network extracts environmental context and dynamically modulates the detection outputs of pre-trained object detectors based on the inferred context, without retraining of the detectors. Our methodology is evaluated on a modified KITTI dataset, in which the camera images and lidar pointclouds are augmented for varying fog levels. Experimental results show that our approach yields an approximately 14% relative improvement over non-adaptive late fusion baselines, achieving a consistent average precision of 56% across different fog levels.
items.author: Arunachalam Venkatachalam, Mhafuzul Islam, Marwan Yusuf, David Van Hamme, Ben Stoffelen, James Foresi
items.summary: The paper introduces a context-aware multimodal late-fusion approach for detecting pedestrians and road users under adverse conditions, integrating a lightweight gating network within a probabilistic calibration framework to adapt sensor fusion per operating context without retraining. This aims to maintain reliability across weather and lighting shifts that degrade pre-trained detectors.
items.reasoning: A well-motivated autonomous-driving safety contribution addressing domain degradation without costly retraining. The Bayesian gating approach is sensible and practical, though late fusion of already-degraded detectors has inherent performance ceilings and the evaluation breadth determines real impact.

items.title: ToF-Wheel Odometry: Navigating Degeneration of Localization With Limited Sensing Capabilities
items.content: arXiv:2610.14590v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Wheel odometry provides an efficient motion prior for ground robots but is prone to transient violations such as wheel slip or terrain-induced tilt. In filtering-based odometry, these violations frequently trigger divergence when they coincide with constrained geometric observability (e.g., featureless corridors). We address this challenge by proposing ToF-Wheel Odometry (TWO), a tightly-coupled filtering framework that integrates wheel kinematics with geometric constraints from Time-of-Flight (ToF) cameras. The primary contribution of this work is a degeneracy-aware, directional covariance-shaping strategy that replaces heuristic online covariance tuning with geometry-conditioned inflation. The core idea is to infer process noise from geometric corrections with a strict reliability check. We decompose the posterior-to-prior correction into a wheel-explainable subspace and an orthogonal remainder. The process covariance is anisotropically adjusted according to the observability of the ToF update: if the geometry is degenerate in non-kinematic directions, the remainder is suppressed as sensor noise; if the geometry is distinct, it is admitted as a valid kinematic violation. Additionally, we introduce an intra-frame feedback loop that retrospectively repairs the process covariance within the current frame to reduce structural lag during bursty disturbances. Extensive experiments on challenging scenarios demonstrate that TWO improves trajectory accuracy and robustness compared to static and adaptive Gaussian filtering, robustly navigating the trade-off between kinematic reliability and limited sensing capabilities.
items.author: Xu Yang, Wenhao Li, Zhengyu Wei, Zening Li, Longxiang Huang, Bo Wang
items.summary: ToF-Wheel Odometry tightly couples wheel kinematics with geometric constraints from Time-of-Flight cameras in a filtering framework for low-cost ground robots. Its main contribution is a degeneracy-aware, directional covariance-shaping strategy that infers process noise from geometry rather than heuristic online tuning, preventing divergence in featureless corridors or during wheel slip. This matters for reliable localization on sensing-limited robots.
items.reasoning: A competent robotics systems contribution with a principled covariance-shaping idea, but the problem setting and methods are relatively narrow and incremental within state estimation research.

Additionally, we introduce an intra-frame feedback loop that retrospectively repairs the process covariance within the current frame to reduce structural lag during bursty disturbances. Extensive experiments on challenging scenarios demonstrate that TWO improves trajectory accuracy and robustness compared to static and adaptive Gaussian filtering, robustly navigating the trade-off between kinematic reliability and limited sensing capabilities.

items.title: Automated carotid artery atherosclerotic inflammation segmentation in PET using MSR-Net
items.content: arXiv:2610.15245v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Objective. To develop an automated method for segmentation and uptake quantification of carotid atherosclerotic inflammation on 64Cu-CANF-comb PET while accounting for partial-volume and tissue-fraction effects. Approach. Synthetic carotid PET images with known fractional-volume ground truth were generated by combining MR-derived high-resolution activity maps with GATE Monte Carlo simulation incorporating major PET physical processes and matched to the Biograph mMR acquisition and reconstruction. A two-stage network first localized the carotid vessel wall from T1-weighted MR and then estimated voxel-wise inflammation fraction from masked PET. Both stages used a multiscale residual (MSR) convolutional backbone. Performance was compared with U-Net, Transformer U-Net, DUCK-Net, and iterative Yang partial-volume correction. Main results. In a two-alternative forced-choice study, five nuclear-medicine physicians identified real images with 54% accuracy (54/100; Wilson 95% CI 0.44-0.63; exact binomial p = 0.48). On 184 simulated test slices from five held-out patients, the proposed method achieved a weighted DSC of 0.79, compared with 0.73 for U-Net, 0.69 for Transformer U-Net, and 0.75 for DUCK-Net, with corresponding HD values of 1.85, 2.29, 2.32, and 2.23 voxels. Patient-cluster bootstrap comparisons favored the proposed method for DSC and HD against all three baselines (Holm-corrected p <= 0.031). Overall ENRMSE was 0.24 versus 0.59, 0.68, and 0.59 for the three DL baselines and 0.57 for iterative Yang. In seven patients, corrected SUV showed a positive association with MR-derived lipid-rich/necrotic core with hemorrhage. Significance. The proposed framework improved carotid PET segmentation and uptake quantification under simulated conditions. The patient analysis is preliminary and requires external validation with biological reference standards before clinical deployment.

items.title: Visual Sevoing from Lines
items.content: arXiv:2610.18363v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In this work, we present a fundamentally new approach to visual servoing using lines. It is based on a theoretical and geometrical study of the main line representations which allowed us to define a new representation, the so-called binormalized Plucker coordinates. They are particularly well suited to visual servoing. Indeed, they allow the definition of a proper image line alignment concept. The control law which realizes such an alignment has moreover several properties: partial decoupling between rotation and translation, analytical inversion of the motion equations and global asymptotic stability conditions. This control law was validated both in simulation and experimentally in the specific case of an orthogonal trihedron.

Despite appearing as a fresh arXiv cross-post, this is classic work from the visual servoing literature by well-known researchers.

items.title: C2Flight: A Closed-Loop Co-Simulation Framework for Early-Stage Evaluation of Heterogeneous UAV Computing Systems
items.content: arXiv:2610.14715v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Early-stage design of heterogeneous UAV computing systems requires evaluating how algorithm, hardware, communication, and system topology affect closed-loop flight before the complete system is available. However, design choices interact through the robotic feedback loop, making task performance difficult to predict from isolated component metrics, while existing execution-driven approaches postpone system-level design feedback until the computing system is integrated. This work presents C2Flight, a closed-loop co-simulation framework that represents target systems as parameterized dataflow graphs and integrates models of hardware under design with independently accessible physical hardware through a unified node interface. Its graph runtime captures the combined effects of buffering, activation, resource sharing, communication, and local timing on closed-loop flight behavior. Validation against onboard and wireless offboard physical computing pipelines confirms its timing fidelity and closed-loop prediction accuracy. Two case studies demonstrate early-stage exploration of deployment and accelerator bit-width choices. These results show that C2Flight exposes system-level design trade-offs before full-system integration, enabling rapid early-stage design refinement.

items.title: Edge-Native Temporal--Graph Dual-Expert Inference for Dexterous Grasp Classification
items.content: arXiv:2610.14926v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multi-finger hands contact objects at different times, so a global close command can overload early-contact fingers while others are still moving. Dense tactile arrays address this problem but add hardware, calibration, bandwidth, and computation. We present an edge-native pipeline that uses only built-in joint-angle and pre-use-calibrated actuator-load feedback to recognize the grasped object and predict an independent Stop event for each finger. Four samples and their first differences form a 4-by-20 contact-evolution window. At its core is a heterogeneous dual-expert architecture, termed DualExpert, that assigns complementary tasks to a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and a Finger Graph Filter Network (FGFN). The TCN models short-term contact evolution and supplies all five Stop probabilities, while the FGFN encodes finger topology and contributes only to object classification. Fixed 0.7/0.3 class-probability fusion reaches 93.78\% trajectory-level classification accuracy on 225 held-out trials, improving the standalone TCN and FGFN by 4.00 and 2.22 percentage points, respectively. The TCN Stop path attains 95.25\% F1. The dataset contains 1,500 automatically collected trajectories from five object instances. In Flash deployment, mixed accelerator execution retains 93.78\% classification accuracy and 94.84\% Stop F1 with 2.890~ms mean inference time and 9.172~ms mean sample-to-stop latency. Across 50 physical trials, the system achieves 96.00\% recognition and 98.00\% grasp success while the complete embedded board draws approximately 0.80~W.

A dual-expert architecture pairs a Temporal Convolutional Network for short-term contact dynamics with a Finger Graph Filter Network over finger relations, processing a compact 4-by-20 contact-evolution window. It prevents overloading early-contact fingers during multi-finger grasps without extra hardware.

items.title: Reinforcement Learning Based Heterogeneous Task Allocation Under Spatio-Temporal Environmental Uncertainty for Multi-Robot Teams
items.content: arXiv:2610.15237v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) have been increasingly deployed to perform different kinds of maritime tasks in recent years, which motivates the need for a reliable task allocation policy that can adapt to heterogeneous tasks and maritime disturbances. In this work, we formulate a multi-robot task allocation problem in which a team of ASVs with heterogeneous capabilities needs to complete tasks of different types and appearance times under unknown stochastic spatio-temporal uncertainties from maritime disturbances. We propose a decentralized Reinforcement Learning (RL) based policy network that is trained to be robust towards uncertainty-induced observation deviations, and is able to perform individual decision making that leads to efficient execution behaviors toward heterogeneous task requirements. We evaluate the proposed policy and four baseline methods in simulated experiments with varied proportions of different tasks types, numbers of tasks, robot species and robots per species. Experiment results show that our proposed policy achieves the lowest makespan and can be deployed to address scenarios with 100 robots and 400 tasks.

A reinforcement learning policy network is trained to be robust to uncertainty-induced observation deviations and to make effective individual decisions.
items.reasoning: Decentralized RL for heterogeneous maritime task allocation under uncertainty is a solid applied contribution with a well-motivated problem formulation. However, decentralized multi-robot RL task allocation is a well-trodden area, and the abstract suggests standard policy-network methods rather than a fundamentally new technique, limiting its research-level impact.

items.title: Multimodal Sensor-Gated Mid-Air Launch and Vision-Based Recovery of a Child UAV on a Hovering Mothership Drone
items.content: arXiv:2610.15740v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Launching a micro unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) from a hovering carrier and recovering it in flight requires reliable confirmation that the child is securely seated before the carrier is allowed to descend. This is challenging because vision provides relative guidance but does not directly indicate load transfer, and a downward-facing camera can lose its fiducial near touchdown. This letter presents a mothership-child quadrotor system in which mission transitions are gated by complementary nonvisual sensing. An upward-facing single-beam LiDAR on the recovery deck provides a binary occupancy state using hysteresis and a debounce interval derived from the child's occluding footprint and crossing speed; real-time kinematic (RTK) positioning conditions the carrier hover; and carrier thrust provides a proprioceptive indication of load transfer. In ten outdoor missions using an F450-class mothership and a Q250-class child with camera-guided recovery, nine completed successfully while RTK-fixed positioning was maintained through release and capture. A complementary MuJoCo study of fully autonomous fiducial-based recovery achieved touchdown 0.077 m from the deck center, while marker detection was lost within the final approximately 0.2 m above the docked configuration. In simulation, carrier thrust changed by -17.0 N at release and +17.3 N at capture, agreeing within 6% with the child's 18.0 N hover thrust. The results support a sensing architecture in which vision guides the approach, while range and proprioceptive information corroborate the final docking decision.

items.title: Behavioural self-monitoring for autonomous earth observation agents: The attribute reliability monitor (ARM)
items.content: arXiv:2610.18548v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language and vision language models can support autonomous systems, but changing operating conditions may compromise the reliability of their semantic outputs. This work introduces the Attribute Reliability Monitor (ARM), a framework that accumulates evidence of suspicion over time to assess individual semantic attributes. ARM accommodates different detectors and temporal monitoring methods, while leaving intervention policies to the consuming system. An initial implementation was evaluated using a specialized vision language model developed for satellite thermal infrared imagery. Monitoring followed a black box approach, using only observable responses without access to internal model states, confidence scores, or external reference answers. Under controlled input degradation, disagreement between responses provided evidence for selective suspension of attributes. The results illustrate how external behavioral monitoring can inform continued use of model outputs, while distinguishing operational suspicion from semantic correctness.

items.title: Assessing the Quality of Concrete Scenarios Generated from Scenario Classes for Automated Driving
items.content: arXiv:2610.18169v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A scenario-based development approach has become state of the art for automated driving systems. Once a set of scenario classes covering the operational design domain is available, concrete scenarios are generated from these scenario classes, e.g., to be used for hazard analysis and risk assessment or for the system's verification and validation. For such applications, a high diversity among the generated concrete scenarios is paramount. The question arises how the quality of collections of concrete scenarios can be assessed in such a setting. In this work, we aggregate scenario distance measures into so-called quality functions that quantify the diversity of concrete scenario collections in the context of automated driving. In particular, we consider the case where scenario classes are formalized as constraint systems and the associated concrete scenario space is not explicitly known. Based on a set of desired properties we construct candidates for such quality functions and give proofs for their property fulfillment. To show the practical relevance of quality functions, we perform a variety of experiments in the context of an abstract scenario-based virtual verification toolchain for automated driving systems. More specifically, we use quality functions to compare the effectiveness of variation methods for sampling, examine the choice of different scenario distance measures, and investigate the effects of temporal aspects on concrete scenario collection quality.

items.summary: The paper proposes quality functions that aggregate scenario distance measures to quantify the diversity of concrete scenario collections generated from scenario classes for automated driving safety validation. High diversity among generated scenarios is essential for hazard analysis and verification coverage of the operational design domain. The work formalizes how to assess whether generated scenario sets are adequate for these tasks.

However, it is an incremental measurement-methodology contribution without deep learning novelty.
